body.name: Assam Flood Emergency
body.tagline: Brahmaputra Basin Monsoonal Inundation & Embankment Breach
body.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall (>220mm/24h) causes severe flooding across Kamrup, Cachar, Barpeta, and Dibrugarh. 4.2M people affected with critical waterlogging, cut-off villages, and washed-away bridges.
body.notes: Prioritize high-capacity dewatering pumps from neighboring West Bengal & Bihar depots. Rescue boats and NDRF teams urgently required.

body.name: Rajasthan Heatwave & Drought
body.tagline: Severe Thar Desert Thermal Anomaly & Groundwater Depletion
body.description: Sustained maximum temperatures exceeding 48.5°C across Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, and Churu. Acute drinking water shortages, rural agricultural distress, and heatstroke casualties.
body.notes: Emergency deployment of water tankers and electrolyte supplies. Surplus assets mobilized from northern plains depots.

body.name: Gujarat Coastal Cyclone Preparation
body.tagline: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Approaching Saurashtra & Kutch
body.description: Category-4 equivalent Arabian Sea cyclone generating sustained winds of 165 km/h, 4-meter tidal surges, and heavy squalls threatening coastal habitations in Kutch, Jamnagar, and Surat.
body.notes: Pre-position evacuation assets, portable generator shelters, and medical trauma teams prior to storm landfall.

body.name: Multi-State Monsoon Emergency
body.tagline: Compounding Inter-Regional Deluges Across Eastern & Southern Belts
body.description: Simultaneous flash floods in Assam, embankment breaches in North Bihar (Katihar, Muzaffarpur), debris flows in Wayanad (Kerala), and coastal surges in Odisha create severe competition for national stockpiles.
body.notes: Tests multi-objective allocation under extreme national scarcity. PuLP balances fairness, transit delays, and life-safety priority.

body.title: ClimateShield AI Methodology, Mathematical Formulation & Constraints

sections.title: 1. Multi-Hazard Risk Scoring Formulation
sections.summary: Hazard-specific normalized scoring (0–100) integrated across four primary hazards: Floods, Heatwaves, Droughts, and Cyclones.

variables.name: P_h
variables.desc: Hazard Probability index [0.0 - 1.0] derived from meteorological signatures

variables.name: I_h
variables.desc: Hazard Intensity index [0.0 - 1.0] scaled to threshold extremes

sections.aggregation_method: R_agg = Max_h(R_h) + 0.20 * (1 - Max_h/100) * Sum_{h != max}(R_h). Avoids double counting while capturing compounded multi-hazard stress.

sections.title: 2. AI/ML Time-Series Forecasting
sections.summary: L2-regularized Ridge Autoregressive Model with rolling multi-day meteorological windows (rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity).
features: Lagged risk indicators: t-1, t-2, t-3
3-day rolling mean & standard deviation of calculated risk
3-day rolling precipitation, temperature, and wind extremes

validation.metrics_calculated: R², Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
validation.uncertainty_intervals: Empirical Gaussian confidence bounds scaled by sqrt(t) horizon step

sections.title: 3. Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (PuLP MILP)
sections.summary: Authoritative optimization engine solving multi-commodity network flow with priority penalties and capacity limits.
sections.objective_function: Min sum(w_unmet * p_k * S_{j,k}) + sum(w_cost * cost_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_delay * time_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_move * X_{i,j,k})
hard_constraints: Donor Minimum Reserve: sum_j X_{i,j,k} <= Available_{i,k} - MinReserve_{i,k}
Destination Demand Balance: LocalUsable_{j,k} + sum_i X_{i,j,k} + S_{j,k} >= Demand_{j,k}
Budget Ceiling: sum_{i,j,k} (Cost_{i,j,k} * X_{i,j,k}) <= Budget_Limit
Hazard-Resource Suitability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if resource k not compatible with recipient hazard
Network Reachability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if travel_time_{i,j} > MaxHours or route is blocked
Integrality: X_{i,j,k} in Integers >= 0, S_{j,k} in Integers >= 0

sections.title: 5. Assumptions & Prototype Disclaimers
items: All Indian regional climate metrics and district records are reproducible synthetic profiles for research and decision-support demonstration.
Road travel times assume an average emergency relief convoy speed of 50 km/h over highway corridors.
No live satellite weather feeds or real-time GPS tracking data is claimed; all results are generated transparently by the local Python optimization backend.

observations.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

body.agency: India Meteorological Department (Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt. of India)
body.api_key_source: IMD_API_KEY environment variable (Optional for NDSAP data.gov.in gateway)

imd_color_code_system.Yellow: Watch (Be Updated — Isolated Heavy Rain / Heat / Squall)
imd_color_code_system.Orange: Alert (Be Prepared — Very Heavy Rain / Severe Heatwave)
imd_color_code_system.Red: Warning (Take Action — Extremely Heavy Rain / Super Cyclone / Extreme Heat)

body.investigation_summary: Official IMD services use a combination of Open Government Data (data.gov.in) REST gateways requiring registered NDSAP tokens, and public AWS portal feeds. ClimateShield AI integrates Open-Meteo High-Resolution WMO weather models for continuous, zero-latency real-time coverage across all 82 Indian districts, while classifying observations strictly according to official IMD color warning thresholds (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red).

endpoints.purpose: National radar mosaics, satellite IR feeds, and cyclone bulletins

endpoints.endpoint_name: IMD City Weather Observation Station System
endpoints.purpose: Historical and real-time AWS (Automatic Weather Station) ground observations

body.name: Assam Flood Emergency
body.tagline: Brahmaputra Basin Monsoonal Inundation & Embankment Breach
body.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall (>220mm/24h) causes severe flooding across Kamrup, Cachar, Barpeta, and Dibrugarh. 4.2M people affected with critical waterlogging, cut-off villages, and washed-away bridges.
body.notes: Prioritize high-capacity dewatering pumps from neighboring West Bengal & Bihar depots. Rescue boats and NDRF teams urgently required.

body.name: Rajasthan Heatwave & Drought
body.tagline: Severe Thar Desert Thermal Anomaly & Groundwater Depletion
body.description: Sustained maximum temperatures exceeding 48.5°C across Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, and Churu. Acute drinking water shortages, rural agricultural distress, and heatstroke casualties.
body.notes: Emergency deployment of water tankers and electrolyte supplies. Surplus assets mobilized from northern plains depots.

body.name: Gujarat Coastal Cyclone Preparation
body.tagline: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Approaching Saurashtra & Kutch
body.description: Category-4 equivalent Arabian Sea cyclone generating sustained winds of 165 km/h, 4-meter tidal surges, and heavy squalls threatening coastal habitations in Kutch, Jamnagar, and Surat.
body.notes: Pre-position evacuation assets, portable generator shelters, and medical trauma teams prior to storm landfall.

body.name: Multi-State Monsoon Emergency
body.tagline: Compounding Inter-Regional Deluges Across Eastern & Southern Belts
body.description: Simultaneous flash floods in Assam, embankment breaches in North Bihar (Katihar, Muzaffarpur), debris flows in Wayanad (Kerala), and coastal surges in Odisha create severe competition for national stockpiles.
body.notes: Tests multi-objective allocation under extreme national scarcity. PuLP balances fairness, transit delays, and life-safety priority.

body.title: ClimateShield AI Methodology, Mathematical Formulation & Constraints

sections.title: 1. Multi-Hazard Risk Scoring Formulation
sections.summary: Hazard-specific normalized scoring (0–100) integrated across four primary hazards: Floods, Heatwaves, Droughts, and Cyclones.

variables.name: P_h
variables.desc: Hazard Probability index [0.0 - 1.0] derived from meteorological signatures

variables.name: I_h
variables.desc: Hazard Intensity index [0.0 - 1.0] scaled to threshold extremes

sections.aggregation_method: R_agg = Max_h(R_h) + 0.20 * (1 - Max_h/100) * Sum_{h != max}(R_h). Avoids double counting while capturing compounded multi-hazard stress.

sections.title: 2. AI/ML Time-Series Forecasting
sections.summary: L2-regularized Ridge Autoregressive Model with rolling multi-day meteorological windows (rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity).
features: Lagged risk indicators: t-1, t-2, t-3
3-day rolling mean & standard deviation of calculated risk
3-day rolling precipitation, temperature, and wind extremes

validation.metrics_calculated: R², Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
validation.uncertainty_intervals: Empirical Gaussian confidence bounds scaled by sqrt(t) horizon step

sections.title: 3. Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (PuLP MILP)
sections.summary: Authoritative optimization engine solving multi-commodity network flow with priority penalties and capacity limits.
sections.objective_function: Min sum(w_unmet * p_k * S_{j,k}) + sum(w_cost * cost_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_delay * time_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_move * X_{i,j,k})
hard_constraints: Donor Minimum Reserve: sum_j X_{i,j,k} <= Available_{i,k} - MinReserve_{i,k}
Destination Demand Balance: LocalUsable_{j,k} + sum_i X_{i,j,k} + S_{j,k} >= Demand_{j,k}
Budget Ceiling: sum_{i,j,k} (Cost_{i,j,k} * X_{i,j,k}) <= Budget_Limit
Hazard-Resource Suitability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if resource k not compatible with recipient hazard
Network Reachability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if travel_time_{i,j} > MaxHours or route is blocked
Integrality: X_{i,j,k} in Integers >= 0, S_{j,k} in Integers >= 0

sections.title: 5. Assumptions & Prototype Disclaimers
items: All Indian regional climate metrics and district records are reproducible synthetic profiles for research and decision-support demonstration.
Road travel times assume an average emergency relief convoy speed of 50 km/h over highway corridors.
No live satellite weather feeds or real-time GPS tracking data is claimed; all results are generated transparently by the local Python optimization backend.

body.api_key_source: IMD_API_KEY environment variable (Optional for NDSAP data.gov.in gateway)

imd_color_code_system.Yellow: Watch (Be Updated — Isolated Heavy Rain / Heat / Squall)
imd_color_code_system.Orange: Alert (Be Prepared — Very Heavy Rain / Severe Heatwave)
imd_color_code_system.Red: Warning (Take Action — Extremely Heavy Rain / Super Cyclone / Extreme Heat)

body.investigation_summary: Official IMD services use a combination of Open Government Data (data.gov.in) REST gateways requiring registered NDSAP tokens, and public AWS portal feeds. ClimateShield AI integrates Open-Meteo High-Resolution WMO weather models for continuous, zero-latency real-time coverage across all 82 Indian districts, while classifying observations strictly according to official IMD color warning thresholds (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red).

endpoints.purpose: National radar mosaics, satellite IR feeds, and cyclone bulletins

endpoints.endpoint_name: IMD City Weather Observation Station System
endpoints.purpose: Historical and real-time AWS (Automatic Weather Station) ground observations

body.name: Assam Flood Emergency
body.tagline: Brahmaputra Basin Monsoonal Inundation & Embankment Breach
body.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall (>220mm/24h) causes severe flooding across Kamrup, Cachar, Barpeta, and Dibrugarh. 4.2M people affected with critical waterlogging, cut-off villages, and washed-away bridges.
body.notes: Prioritize high-capacity dewatering pumps from neighboring West Bengal & Bihar depots. Rescue boats and NDRF teams urgently required.

body.name: Rajasthan Heatwave & Drought
body.tagline: Severe Thar Desert Thermal Anomaly & Groundwater Depletion
body.description: Sustained maximum temperatures exceeding 48.5°C across Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, and Churu. Acute drinking water shortages, rural agricultural distress, and heatstroke casualties.
body.notes: Emergency deployment of water tankers and electrolyte supplies. Surplus assets mobilized from northern plains depots.

body.name: Gujarat Coastal Cyclone Preparation
body.tagline: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Approaching Saurashtra & Kutch
body.description: Category-4 equivalent Arabian Sea cyclone generating sustained winds of 165 km/h, 4-meter tidal surges, and heavy squalls threatening coastal habitations in Kutch, Jamnagar, and Surat.
body.notes: Pre-position evacuation assets, portable generator shelters, and medical trauma teams prior to storm landfall.

body.name: Multi-State Monsoon Emergency
body.tagline: Compounding Inter-Regional Deluges Across Eastern & Southern Belts
body.description: Simultaneous flash floods in Assam, embankment breaches in North Bihar (Katihar, Muzaffarpur), debris flows in Wayanad (Kerala), and coastal surges in Odisha create severe competition for national stockpiles.
body.notes: Tests multi-objective allocation under extreme national scarcity. PuLP balances fairness, transit delays, and life-safety priority.

body.title: ClimateShield AI Methodology, Mathematical Formulation & Constraints

sections.title: 1. Multi-Hazard Risk Scoring Formulation
sections.summary: Hazard-specific normalized scoring (0–100) integrated across four primary hazards: Floods, Heatwaves, Droughts, and Cyclones.

variables.name: P_h
variables.desc: Hazard Probability index [0.0 - 1.0] derived from meteorological signatures

variables.name: I_h
variables.desc: Hazard Intensity index [0.0 - 1.0] scaled to threshold extremes

sections.aggregation_method: R_agg = Max_h(R_h) + 0.20 * (1 - Max_h/100) * Sum_{h != max}(R_h). Avoids double counting while capturing compounded multi-hazard stress.

sections.title: 2. AI/ML Time-Series Forecasting
sections.summary: L2-regularized Ridge Autoregressive Model with rolling multi-day meteorological windows (rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity).
features: Lagged risk indicators: t-1, t-2, t-3
3-day rolling mean & standard deviation of calculated risk
3-day rolling precipitation, temperature, and wind extremes

validation.metrics_calculated: R², Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
validation.uncertainty_intervals: Empirical Gaussian confidence bounds scaled by sqrt(t) horizon step

sections.title: 3. Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (PuLP MILP)
sections.summary: Authoritative optimization engine solving multi-commodity network flow with priority penalties and capacity limits.
sections.objective_function: Min sum(w_unmet * p_k * S_{j,k}) + sum(w_cost * cost_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_delay * time_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_move * X_{i,j,k})
hard_constraints: Donor Minimum Reserve: sum_j X_{i,j,k} <= Available_{i,k} - MinReserve_{i,k}
Destination Demand Balance: LocalUsable_{j,k} + sum_i X_{i,j,k} + S_{j,k} >= Demand_{j,k}
Budget Ceiling: sum_{i,j,k} (Cost_{i,j,k} * X_{i,j,k}) <= Budget_Limit
Hazard-Resource Suitability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if resource k not compatible with recipient hazard
Network Reachability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if travel_time_{i,j} > MaxHours or route is blocked
Integrality: X_{i,j,k} in Integers >= 0, S_{j,k} in Integers >= 0

sections.title: 5. Assumptions & Prototype Disclaimers
items: All Indian regional climate metrics and district records are reproducible synthetic profiles for research and decision-support demonstration.
Road travel times assume an average emergency relief convoy speed of 50 km/h over highway corridors.
No live satellite weather feeds or real-time GPS tracking data is claimed; all results are generated transparently by the local Python optimization backend.

summary.data_source: Open-Meteo High-Resolution Numerical Weather Prediction API

observations.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

body.agency: India Meteorological Department (Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt. of India)
body.api_key_source: IMD_API_KEY environment variable (Optional for NDSAP data.gov.in gateway)

imd_color_code_system.Yellow: Watch (Be Updated — Isolated Heavy Rain / Heat / Squall)
imd_color_code_system.Orange: Alert (Be Prepared — Very Heavy Rain / Severe Heatwave)
imd_color_code_system.Red: Warning (Take Action — Extremely Heavy Rain / Super Cyclone / Extreme Heat)

body.investigation_summary: Official IMD services use a combination of Open Government Data (data.gov.in) REST gateways requiring registered NDSAP tokens, and public AWS portal feeds. ClimateShield AI integrates Open-Meteo High-Resolution WMO weather models for continuous, zero-latency real-time coverage across all 82 Indian districts, while classifying observations strictly according to official IMD color warning thresholds (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red).

endpoints.purpose: National radar mosaics, satellite IR feeds, and cyclone bulletins

endpoints.endpoint_name: IMD City Weather Observation Station System
endpoints.purpose: Historical and real-time AWS (Automatic Weather Station) ground observations

body.name: Assam Flood Emergency
body.tagline: Brahmaputra Basin Monsoonal Inundation & Embankment Breach
body.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall (>220mm/24h) causes severe flooding across Kamrup, Cachar, Barpeta, and Dibrugarh. 4.2M people affected with critical waterlogging, cut-off villages, and washed-away bridges.
body.notes: Prioritize high-capacity dewatering pumps from neighboring West Bengal & Bihar depots. Rescue boats and NDRF teams urgently required.

body.name: Rajasthan Heatwave & Drought
body.tagline: Severe Thar Desert Thermal Anomaly & Groundwater Depletion
body.description: Sustained maximum temperatures exceeding 48.5°C across Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, and Churu. Acute drinking water shortages, rural agricultural distress, and heatstroke casualties.
body.notes: Emergency deployment of water tankers and electrolyte supplies. Surplus assets mobilized from northern plains depots.

body.name: Gujarat Coastal Cyclone Preparation
body.tagline: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Approaching Saurashtra & Kutch
body.description: Category-4 equivalent Arabian Sea cyclone generating sustained winds of 165 km/h, 4-meter tidal surges, and heavy squalls threatening coastal habitations in Kutch, Jamnagar, and Surat.
body.notes: Pre-position evacuation assets, portable generator shelters, and medical trauma teams prior to storm landfall.

body.name: Multi-State Monsoon Emergency
body.tagline: Compounding Inter-Regional Deluges Across Eastern & Southern Belts
body.description: Simultaneous flash floods in Assam, embankment breaches in North Bihar (Katihar, Muzaffarpur), debris flows in Wayanad (Kerala), and coastal surges in Odisha create severe competition for national stockpiles.
body.notes: Tests multi-objective allocation under extreme national scarcity. PuLP balances fairness, transit delays, and life-safety priority.

body.title: ClimateShield AI Methodology, Mathematical Formulation & Constraints

sections.title: 1. Multi-Hazard Risk Scoring Formulation
sections.summary: Hazard-specific normalized scoring (0–100) integrated across four primary hazards: Floods, Heatwaves, Droughts, and Cyclones.

variables.name: P_h
variables.desc: Hazard Probability index [0.0 - 1.0] derived from meteorological signatures

variables.name: I_h
variables.desc: Hazard Intensity index [0.0 - 1.0] scaled to threshold extremes

sections.aggregation_method: R_agg = Max_h(R_h) + 0.20 * (1 - Max_h/100) * Sum_{h != max}(R_h). Avoids double counting while capturing compounded multi-hazard stress.

sections.title: 2. AI/ML Time-Series Forecasting
sections.summary: L2-regularized Ridge Autoregressive Model with rolling multi-day meteorological windows (rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity).
features: Lagged risk indicators: t-1, t-2, t-3
3-day rolling mean & standard deviation of calculated risk
3-day rolling precipitation, temperature, and wind extremes

validation.metrics_calculated: R², Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
validation.uncertainty_intervals: Empirical Gaussian confidence bounds scaled by sqrt(t) horizon step

sections.title: 3. Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (PuLP MILP)
sections.summary: Authoritative optimization engine solving multi-commodity network flow with priority penalties and capacity limits.
sections.objective_function: Min sum(w_unmet * p_k * S_{j,k}) + sum(w_cost * cost_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_delay * time_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_move * X_{i,j,k})
hard_constraints: Donor Minimum Reserve: sum_j X_{i,j,k} <= Available_{i,k} - MinReserve_{i,k}
Destination Demand Balance: LocalUsable_{j,k} + sum_i X_{i,j,k} + S_{j,k} >= Demand_{j,k}
Budget Ceiling: sum_{i,j,k} (Cost_{i,j,k} * X_{i,j,k}) <= Budget_Limit
Hazard-Resource Suitability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if resource k not compatible with recipient hazard
Network Reachability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if travel_time_{i,j} > MaxHours or route is blocked
Integrality: X_{i,j,k} in Integers >= 0, S_{j,k} in Integers >= 0

sections.title: 5. Assumptions & Prototype Disclaimers
items: All Indian regional climate metrics and district records are reproducible synthetic profiles for research and decision-support demonstration.
Road travel times assume an average emergency relief convoy speed of 50 km/h over highway corridors.
No live satellite weather feeds or real-time GPS tracking data is claimed; all results are generated transparently by the local Python optimization backend.

body.investigation_summary: Official IMD services use a combination of Open Government Data (data.gov.in) REST gateways requiring registered NDSAP tokens, and public AWS portal feeds. ClimateShield AI integrates Open-Meteo High-Resolution WMO weather models for continuous, zero-latency real-time coverage across all 82 Indian districts, while classifying observations strictly according to official IMD color warning thresholds (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red).

endpoints.purpose: National radar mosaics, satellite IR feeds, and cyclone bulletins

endpoints.endpoint_name: IMD City Weather Observation Station System
endpoints.purpose: Historical and real-time AWS (Automatic Weather Station) ground observations

body.name: Assam Flood Emergency
body.tagline: Brahmaputra Basin Monsoonal Inundation & Embankment Breach
body.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall (>220mm/24h) causes severe flooding across Kamrup, Cachar, Barpeta, and Dibrugarh. 4.2M people affected with critical waterlogging, cut-off villages, and washed-away bridges.
body.notes: Prioritize high-capacity dewatering pumps from neighboring West Bengal & Bihar depots. Rescue boats and NDRF teams urgently required.

body.name: Rajasthan Heatwave & Drought
body.tagline: Severe Thar Desert Thermal Anomaly & Groundwater Depletion
body.description: Sustained maximum temperatures exceeding 48.5°C across Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, and Churu. Acute drinking water shortages, rural agricultural distress, and heatstroke casualties.
body.notes: Emergency deployment of water tankers and electrolyte supplies. Surplus assets mobilized from northern plains depots.

body.name: Gujarat Coastal Cyclone Preparation
body.tagline: Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm Approaching Saurashtra & Kutch
body.description: Category-4 equivalent Arabian Sea cyclone generating sustained winds of 165 km/h, 4-meter tidal surges, and heavy squalls threatening coastal habitations in Kutch, Jamnagar, and Surat.
body.notes: Pre-position evacuation assets, portable generator shelters, and medical trauma teams prior to storm landfall.

body.name: Multi-State Monsoon Emergency
body.tagline: Compounding Inter-Regional Deluges Across Eastern & Southern Belts
body.description: Simultaneous flash floods in Assam, embankment breaches in North Bihar (Katihar, Muzaffarpur), debris flows in Wayanad (Kerala), and coastal surges in Odisha create severe competition for national stockpiles.
body.notes: Tests multi-objective allocation under extreme national scarcity. PuLP balances fairness, transit delays, and life-safety priority.

body.title: ClimateShield AI Methodology, Mathematical Formulation & Constraints

sections.title: 1. Multi-Hazard Risk Scoring Formulation
sections.summary: Hazard-specific normalized scoring (0–100) integrated across four primary hazards: Floods, Heatwaves, Droughts, and Cyclones.

variables.name: P_h
variables.desc: Hazard Probability index [0.0 - 1.0] derived from meteorological signatures

variables.name: I_h
variables.desc: Hazard Intensity index [0.0 - 1.0] scaled to threshold extremes

sections.aggregation_method: R_agg = Max_h(R_h) + 0.20 * (1 - Max_h/100) * Sum_{h != max}(R_h). Avoids double counting while capturing compounded multi-hazard stress.

sections.title: 2. AI/ML Time-Series Forecasting
sections.summary: L2-regularized Ridge Autoregressive Model with rolling multi-day meteorological windows (rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity).
features: Lagged risk indicators: t-1, t-2, t-3
3-day rolling mean & standard deviation of calculated risk
3-day rolling precipitation, temperature, and wind extremes

validation.metrics_calculated: R², Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
validation.uncertainty_intervals: Empirical Gaussian confidence bounds scaled by sqrt(t) horizon step

sections.title: 3. Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (PuLP MILP)
sections.summary: Authoritative optimization engine solving multi-commodity network flow with priority penalties and capacity limits.
sections.objective_function: Min sum(w_unmet * p_k * S_{j,k}) + sum(w_cost * cost_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_delay * time_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_move * X_{i,j,k})
hard_constraints: Donor Minimum Reserve: sum_j X_{i,j,k} <= Available_{i,k} - MinReserve_{i,k}
Destination Demand Balance: LocalUsable_{j,k} + sum_i X_{i,j,k} + S_{j,k} >= Demand_{j,k}
Budget Ceiling: sum_{i,j,k} (Cost_{i,j,k} * X_{i,j,k}) <= Budget_Limit
Hazard-Resource Suitability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if resource k not compatible with recipient hazard
Network Reachability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if travel_time_{i,j} > MaxHours or route is blocked
Integrality: X_{i,j,k} in Integers >= 0, S_{j,k} in Integers >= 0

sections.title: 5. Assumptions & Prototype Disclaimers
items: All Indian regional climate metrics and district records are reproducible synthetic profiles for research and decision-support demonstration.
Road travel times assume an average emergency relief convoy speed of 50 km/h over highway corridors.
No live satellite weather feeds or real-time GPS tracking data is claimed; all results are generated transparently by the local Python optimization backend.

body.investigation_summary: Official IMD services use a combination of Open Government Data (data.gov.in) REST gateways requiring registered NDSAP tokens, and public AWS portal feeds. ClimateShield AI integrates Open-Meteo High-Resolution WMO weather models for continuous, zero-latency real-time coverage across all 82 Indian districts, while classifying observations strictly according to official IMD color warning thresholds (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red).

scenario.name: Multi-State Monsoon Emergency
scenario.tagline: Compounding Inter-Regional Deluges Across Eastern & Southern Belts
scenario.description: Simultaneous flash floods in Assam, embankment breaches in North Bihar (Katihar, Muzaffarpur), debris flows in Wayanad (Kerala), and coastal surges in Odisha create severe competition for national stockpiles.
scenario.notes: Tests multi-objective allocation under extreme national scarcity. PuLP balances fairness, transit delays, and life-safety priority.

body.name: Assam Flood Emergency
body.tagline: Brahmaputra Basin Monsoonal Inundation & Embankment Breach
body.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall (>220mm/24h) causes severe flooding across Kamrup, Cachar, Barpeta, and Dibrugarh. 4.2M people affected with critical waterlogging, cut-off villages, and washed-away bridges.
body.notes: Prioritize high-capacity dewatering pumps from neighboring West Bengal & Bihar depots. Rescue boats and NDRF teams urgently required.

body.name: Rajasthan Heatwave & Drought
body.tagline: Severe Thar Desert Thermal Anomaly & Groundwater Depletion
body.description: Sustained maximum temperatures exceeding 48.5°C across Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, and Churu. Acute drinking water shortages, rural agricultural distress, and heatstroke casualties.
body.notes: Emergency deployment of water tankers and electrolyte supplies. Surplus assets mobilized from northern plains depots.

body.name: Gujarat Coastal Cyclone Preparation

body.notes: Pre-position evacuation assets, portable generator shelters, and medical trauma teams prior to storm landfall.

body.title: ClimateShield AI Methodology, Mathematical Formulation & Constraints

sections.title: 1. Multi-Hazard Risk Scoring Formulation
sections.summary: Hazard-specific normalized scoring (0–100) integrated across four primary hazards: Floods, Heatwaves, Droughts, and Cyclones.

variables.name: P_h
variables.desc: Hazard Probability index [0.0 - 1.0] derived from meteorological signatures

variables.name: I_h
variables.desc: Hazard Intensity index [0.0 - 1.0] scaled to threshold extremes

sections.aggregation_method: R_agg = Max_h(R_h) + 0.20 * (1 - Max_h/100) * Sum_{h != max}(R_h). Avoids double counting while capturing compounded multi-hazard stress.

sections.title: 2. AI/ML Time-Series Forecasting
sections.summary: L2-regularized Ridge Autoregressive Model with rolling multi-day meteorological windows (rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity).
features: Lagged risk indicators: t-1, t-2, t-3
3-day rolling mean & standard deviation of calculated risk
3-day rolling precipitation, temperature, and wind extremes

validation.metrics_calculated: R², Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
validation.uncertainty_intervals: Empirical Gaussian confidence bounds scaled by sqrt(t) horizon step

sections.title: 3. Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (PuLP MILP)
sections.summary: Authoritative optimization engine solving multi-commodity network flow with priority penalties and capacity limits.
sections.objective_function: Min sum(w_unmet * p_k * S_{j,k}) + sum(w_cost * cost_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_delay * time_{i,j} * X_{i,j,k}) + sum(w_move * X_{i,j,k})
hard_constraints: Donor Minimum Reserve: sum_j X_{i,j,k} <= Available_{i,k} - MinReserve_{i,k}
Destination Demand Balance: LocalUsable_{j,k} + sum_i X_{i,j,k} + S_{j,k} >= Demand_{j,k}
Budget Ceiling: sum_{i,j,k} (Cost_{i,j,k} * X_{i,j,k}) <= Budget_Limit
Hazard-Resource Suitability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if resource k not compatible with recipient hazard
Network Reachability: X_{i,j,k} = 0 if travel_time_{i,j} > MaxHours or route is blocked
Integrality: X_{i,j,k} in Integers >= 0, S_{j,k} in Integers >= 0

sections.title: 5. Assumptions & Prototype Disclaimers
items: All Indian regional climate metrics and district records are reproducible synthetic profiles for research and decision-support demonstration.
Road travel times assume an average emergency relief convoy speed of 50 km/h over highway corridors.
No live satellite weather feeds or real-time GPS tracking data is claimed; all results are generated transparently by the local Python optimization backend.

body.investigation_summary: Official IMD services use a combination of Open Government Data (data.gov.in) REST gateways requiring registered NDSAP tokens, and public AWS portal feeds. ClimateShield AI integrates Open-Meteo High-Resolution WMO weather models for continuous, zero-latency real-time coverage across all 82 Indian districts, while classifying observations strictly according to official IMD color warning thresholds (Green/Yellow/Orange/Red).
